name: SIERRA LEONE
lead: Sierra Leone sits on West Africa's coast where rainforests meet dazzling Atlantic beaches. Freetown, the capital, was founded by freed slaves in 1787 — one of history's most extraordinary city stories. Beneath the red soil lie some of the world's finest diamonds, while chimpanzees swing through jungle canopies above turquoise coves.

geo: Sierra Leone packs everything in tightly — thick rainforests in the east, rolling hills in the north crowned by Mount Bintumani, and a coast fringed with white-sand beaches that many travellers call the finest in West Africa.

Freetown sits on one of the world's largest natural deep-water harbours, sheltering ships for centuries. The Gola Rainforest in the south-east is one of the last fragments of the ancient Upper Guinea forest, a biodiversity hotspot millions of years old.
animals: Sierra Leone's forests shelter over 5,500 western chimpanzees — the second-largest wild population in the world. The Tacugama Sanctuary near Freetown rescues orphaned chimps and carefully returns them to the wild.

The tiny pygmy hippopotamus hides along the Moa River — just 200 kg, it lives alone in dense undergrowth unlike its giant cousin. The Gola malimbe, a brilliant red-and-black weaver bird, is found almost nowhere else on Earth.
culture: Krio — a creole born from English, African languages, and Caribbean speech — ties all of Sierra Leone's ethnic groups together. Music fills Freetown's streets: Afrobeat, reggae, and palm-wine guitar blended into something uniquely Salone.

Rice anchors every meal — jollof rice with stew, groundnut soup over white rice, or slow-cooked cassava-leaf sauce. The August Freetown Carnival fills streets with colour, drumming, and dancing long into the warm night.
history: In 1787 British abolitionists settled freed Black people on a peninsula called 'Province of Freedom' — the seed of Freetown. Thousands more freed Africans arrived after Britain banned the slave trade in 1807, making it a great city of liberty.

Diamonds found in 1930 brought wealth and conflict. A brutal civil war (1991–2002) funded by 'blood diamonds' killed 50,000 people. Since peace returned Sierra Leone has rebuilt with remarkable spirit, welcoming visitors to its beaches.
wows: A 969-carat diamond — the Star of Sierra Leone (1972) — is the largest alluvial diamond ever found.
Freetown's harbour is so deep that the world's largest ships anchor without touching the seabed.
A 300-year-old Cotton Tree in the city centre saw freed slaves pray beneath it in 1792.
Krio sounds so close to English that many native speakers can partially understand it.
Tacugama Sanctuary has rehabilitated 100+ chimps and returned some to wild forest.
Tokeh and River No. 2 Beach are listed among Africa's most beautiful — yet barely visited.
Half of Sierra Leone's population is under 19 — one of the world's youngest nations.

myths.fact: The civil war ended in 2002. Freetown is a lively, welcoming city with a growing tourism scene. Check current travel advice as with any destination.
Portuguese explorer Pedro de Sintra named it 'Serra Lyoa' in 1462 for thunder that rumbled like a lion's roar around the hills — not for any lions.
